_design: Steve 2026-10-05: 'Everyone's backstory has a year everything changed before the sky did. Let's have some diversity. Makes things feel not alive.' Problem: (1) every villager gets the IDENTICAL structural beat 'X — that's the year everything changed, before the sky did' (lifeseed.js:204, codex-people.js:152), (2) pools are 6/6/6 so a 12-person village repeats constantly. Fix has two parts: FRAMES (not everyone had a year that changed everything) and DEPTH (pools sized so a full village can draw without replacement). Suggested code changes: (a) events become {t, f} objects; suffix chosen from FRAMES[f] (missing f = classic 'changed'), (b) deal events/wounds/wants from per-game shuffled decks so no two villagers share a beat in one village — extends the existing 'no repeated names or backgrounds within a single game' rule to lifeseed beats. Voice notes: concrete, physical, pre-sky America; placeholders {first} {kin} {town} {place} {workplace} work as today (fillBasic). Bright frames matter: not everyone was broken before the sky — some were fine, which makes the scattering land harder.

_frames.bright: — the last good thing, before the sky did.
_frames.changed: — that's the year everything changed, before the sky did.
_frames.plain: (no suffix — just a fact of the life, stated flat)
_frames.slow: — nothing changed all at once. It just went, before the sky did.
_frames.unfinished: — still unfinished, when the sky did.

events.t: the flood year, when the water took the low road
the winter the {workplace} closed
the fire season that turned the sky orange for a month
the spring the river jumped its banks
the year the mill laid off half the town
the storm that took the power for nine days
the year the {town} plant moved south and took the pensions with it
the drought summer when the wells went brackish
the winter the bridge washed out and nobody fixed it
the year {kin} got sick and the insurance ran out first
the years the {workplace} kept cutting shifts, a few at a time
the slow emptying of {town}, one for-sale sign at a time
the seasons the river ran lower and lower and nobody said it out loud
the years the winters got meaner and the summers got stranger
the long stretch where the money just never quite reached
the summer {first} finally got the old boat running
the year the garden behind the house fed half the block
the winter {kin} taught {first} to read the ice
the fall the {town} team went all the way, and the whole town with it
the spring {first} fixed the roof alone and stood up there watching the weather come in
the letter to {kin} that never got sent
the trip to {place} that kept getting put off
the apology owed to {kin}, still owed
the {workplace} project that was almost done when it all stopped mattering

wants: keep these people fed through winter
learn what the System actually wants
build something that lasts longer than they do
never be helpless like that again
a working stove and a dry roof — {first} doesn't ask for much
to hear {kin}'s voice one more time, even wrong
teach somebody the things {kin} taught them, before it's too late
a map with somewhere on it worth walking to
to stop dreaming about the sirens
one full meal that nobody has to apologize for
find the people from the clearing — all of them
make the {workplace} skills mean something again
a quiet hour that isn't the quiet before something
to be the person people call again
see {place} one more time, the way it was
keep {kin}'s name alive in somebody's mouth
wounds: {first} doesn't talk about the last winter before the scattering.
There is a name {first} won't say out loud anymore.
{first} was supposed to be somewhere else that day.
Somebody {first} loved didn't make it to the clearing.
{first} carries a guilt like a stone in the boot.
The scattering took the one person {first} was keeping alive.
{first} once chose the easy wrong over the hard right, and it cost somebody.
{first} never learned {kin}'s recipe and now nobody can teach it.
{first} froze once, when it mattered most, and remembers the shape of that minute.
There was a dog. {first} doesn't talk about the dog.
{first} laughed at the wrong moment, years ago, and the room went quiet.
The last thing {first} said to {kin} was something small and mean.
{first} knows exactly which shelf the good photos were on. The shelf is gone.
{first} used to be the person people called. Then the calls stopped coming.
{first} sold something that wasn't theirs to sell, back when it seemed fine.
{first} keeps a list of the people they failed. It gets longer, not shorter.
{first} was good at something once. The world stopped needing it.
{first} watched {town} change and said nothing, and that silence has a weight.
